To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there is a need for an international convention to protect the rights of older people, that such a convention should contain specific provisions on older persons, and that the drafting of such a convention should begin with a regional instrument.

the international legal framework for the promotion and protection the rights of older people has been strengthened in recent years, and that there are now several international and regional instruments that are of relevance in this respect, but that the lack of a legally binding international instrument for the protection of older people's rights is an important gap that should be remedied, and that the countries of Latin America and Caribbean should work towards that end.

the international community should approve a convention on the rights and freedoms of older persons, that the convention should be based on the human-rights-based approach, that it should be legally binding, that it should cover both civil and political rights and economic, social and cultural rights, that it should contain specific rights and freedoms that apply exclusively to older persons and that it should include the right to an adequate standard of living.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the rights of older people?

the following issues: the conceptual framework for the analysis of the situation of older persons; the international and regional framework for the promotion and protection for the rights of older people; national legislation for the protection of older persons' rights in Latin America; and the need for and components of a future regional and international convention on the human rights of older persons.
the following issues: 1) What is the current situation of human rights for older persons in Latin American and Caribbean societies?;
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the protection of the human rights of older persons, as of any other group of people, is an essential condition for their full and effective participation in the life of society, as well as for the achievement of social justice.
there is no international legal instrument that protects the rights of older people, but there are a number of national and international norms and conventions that protect their rights.
the protection of the older persons' rights has been a subject of concern for the international community since the 1990s.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is the first book that has been written on the rights of the older people.
the protection of the older persons rights is an important issue in the region and that it needs a more detailed analysis and discussion.

this publication seeks to contribute to a process of reflection on the need to protect the rights of older people and to provide a basis for the development of a convention that would be of benefit to all older persons in the region.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to ensure the protection of the human rights of older persons, it is necessary to develop an international instrument that is based on the principles of universality, indivisibility and interdependence, which are the pillars of the international human rights system, and that is capable of addressing the specific situation of older persons.

the protection of the human rights of older persons should be the subject of a convention that is legally binding and universally applicable, and that the Latin American and Caribbean countries should play a leading role in this regard.

the time has come to move beyond the current situation of a patchwork of disparate norms, and that the region is in a good position to play a key role in the development of an internationally binding instrument on older persons' human rights.
